page.layout: One page of text, with a worked fraction example set below the paragraphs. The running head is at the top left and the page number at the top right. The lowest block is a display of sums in lines, with no margin notes.

main_text.p: nit 1 ac 1 4/2 4, quæ per 2 in hanc fractionem rediguntur: 7/1 2
Iam productæ Fractioni adjungo tertiam Fractionem suprà positam sic:

Et dico ter 12 sunt 36, quæ seorsim scribo, ac progredior dicens: quinquies 7 sunt 35, quæ subscripta & per additionem collecta, efficiunt 71. Nunc Denominatorem per alterum multiplico, dicens: quinquies 12 sunt 60, per quæ divido 71, & producitur 1 & undecim 60. Productę [?] fractioni adjungo quartam suprà positam sic:

Et dico ter 60 sunt 180, quæ seorsim scribo, ac pergo dicens: septies 11, sunt 77, quæ subscripta & addita efficiunt 257. Nunc Denominatorem per alterum multiplico, dicens: septies 6, sunt 420, per quæ non possum 257 dividere: linea igitur interjecta, fit fractio sic:

p.i: Aliud exemplum, in quo Fractiones primùm, ut suprà monstratum colliguntur: deinde adduntur.

page.notes: The fraction notation is rendered in plain form ("1 4/2 4" for 14/24, "7/1 2" for 7/12) because stacked fractions do not reproduce well in text. The word "Productę" ends in a ligature that is hard to read, so it is marked [?]. The bottom display is partly set in fraction form and its alignment is approximate. The long s is transcribed as s throughout, so "possum" is printed "posfum" on the scan.
